newsitem.title: USA: Saudis fund White Helmet program for Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: Saudis fund White Helmet program for Palestinians.

text.p: Saudi Arabia has earmarked $3 million for humanitarian projects in Palestinian-controlled areas and Rwanda to be carried out by the White Helmets, an international volunteer corps, programme officials said on Wednesday.

The initiative, designed as a humanitarian counterpart to the blue-helmeted U.N. peacekeeping forces, will train 50 computer instructors in West Bank towns and help rebuild the infrastructure of Gaza City starting in the next few months.

The White Helmets corps was proposed by President Carlos Menem of Argentina in 1993 and endorsed by the U.N. General Assembly the following year. Participating countries recruit their own White Helmet teams to provide quick-response humanitarian services worldwide.

Ambassador-at-large Octavio Frigerio, president of the White Helmets Commission, an Argentine group that coordinates the work of the international volunteers, told reporters that he expected "not less" than 30 or 40 volunteers to train locally recruited Palestinian counterparts.
In Rwanda, a German-financed White Helmet team is being organised to help build homes for refugees returning from neighbouring Zaire.
